title: Stage 7 — Growing the System
goal: Grow the product: authentication, related data, and paginated lists — without restarting.
summary: The finale — add auth, user-scoped data, relationships, and pagination to the same deployed, tested app.

checkpoint.prompt: "Only the owner can delete this workout" is an example of…
checkpoint.explanation: Authentication = identity. Authorization = permissions after identity is known.

checkpoint.prompt: How should passwords be stored in the database?

choices.text: Hashed with a slow algorithm (bcrypt, argon2) — never plain text
Plain text for easy password resets

checkpoint.explanation: Hashing is one-way. If the DB leaks, attackers still can't read passwords.

checkpoint.prompt: Each workout belongs to one user. In the workouts table, `user_id` should…

choices.text: Be optional on every row with no link

checkpoint.explanation: Foreign keys enforce relationships at the database level and enable efficient joins.

checkpoint.prompt: GET /workouts?page=2&limit=20 — what does the API return differently from page 1?

choices.text: The next slice of results (rows 21–40), not the full table

checkpoint.explanation: Pagination limits payload size and query cost. Page + limit (or cursor) select a window of rows.

checkpoint.prompt: You're adding auth, then user-scoped workouts, then pagination. Best workflow?

choices.text: Separate feature branches / PRs — merge auth before building on it

checkpoint.explanation: Incremental merges keep review manageable and let you revert one feature if needed.

checklist.label: Users can sign up / sign in (session or token)
Main records scoped to the signed-in user
Related entity with foreign key (e.g. categories, tags)
List endpoint supports page/limit or cursor
Tests cover auth and at least one new endpoint

questions.prompt: A session cookie after login typically proves…

choices.text: The server recognizes this browser as an authenticated user
The user's password for future requests

questions.explanation: Sessions store server-side state keyed by a cookie. Passwords are not re-sent each request.

questions.prompt: 401 Unauthorized vs 403 Forbidden — which fits "not logged in"?
questions.explanation: 401 = who are you? 403 = I know who you are, but you can't do this.

questions.prompt: One user, many workouts — what relationship is that?
questions.explanation: The "many" side holds the foreign key pointing to the "one" side.

choices.text: Faster responses and less memory when tables grow large
SQL cannot return more than one row

questions.explanation: Pagination keeps payloads bounded. Clients load more as the user scrolls or clicks next.

choices.text: Build, deploy, test, and evolve a full-stack app without restarting
Finish without ever pushing to GitHub

questions.explanation: Breadth + habits + one real repo. Specialization comes in optional later tracks.
